paper_metadata.title: Heterostructural nanolamellar oxide-dispersion-strengthened ferritic alloy with exceptional strength and ductility

evidence.quote: Nanostructured ferritic alloys (NFAs) have demonstrated exceptional mechanical properties (strength and creep resistance) and radiation tolerance.

Here, we report a novel heterostructural nanolamellar ferritic alloy (NLFA) with microcrystalline (MC) domains (~ 35 % of volume fraction) dispersed in an ultrafine-grained (UFG) matrix (~ 500 nm grain size)

Zr doped 14YWT NLFA with a nominal composition of Fe-14Cr-3W-0.4Ti-0.8Zr-0.3Y2O3 (wt%) was prepared by mechanically alloying the mixture of high-purity elemental Fe, Cr, W, Ti, Zr powders (Alfa Aesar, 99.9 % pure, 200 mesh) and Y2O3 nanoparticles (Alfa Aesar, 99.5 % pure, average particle size of 20 nm), followed by a two-step consolidation process.

For the homogeneous alloy, 6 g of powder mixtures and 48 g of hardened steel balls were placed in a hardened steel milling vial, and the mechanical alloying was conducted by a high-energy ball milling process with a rotation speed of 1425 rpm for 24 h in a SPEX 8000D shaker mill inside an argon-filled glove box.
the mechanically alloyed powders were pre-sintered by a high-pressure sintering technique at 800 °C and under a pressure of 4 GPa for 30 min.
the mechanical alloying was conducted by a low-energy ball milling process with a rotation speed of 300 rpm for 50 h in a MiQi QM-QX2L planetary mill.
Then, the mechanically alloyed powders were pre-sintered by a high-pressure sintering technique at 800 °C and under a pressure of 4 GPa for 30 min.

Finally, the two kinds of high-pressure pre-sintered alloys (named as HPed alloy hereafter) were further multi-pass rolled at 800 °C to a total thickness reduction of ~ 85 % (named as HRed alloy hereafter).

evidence.quote: Here, we report a novel heterostructural nanolamellar ferritic alloy (NLFA) with microcrystalline (MC) domains (~ 35 % of volume fraction) dispersed in an ultrafine-grained (UFG) matrix (~ 500 nm grain size)

attributes.size: ~1.5 ± 0.6 μm equivalent diameter on RD-TD, 380 ± 90 nm thickness along ND

evidence.quote: The alloy shows a distinctive heterogeneous single-phase structure with some micrometer-sized lamellar-shaped ferrite grains (with a volume fraction of ~ 35 %) dispersed in the UFG ferrite matrix. These large lamellar-shaped grains are extensively elongated along the rolling direction with an average equivalent diameter of ~ 1.5 ± 0.6 μm on the rolling direction (RD) - transverse direction (TD) plane (Fig. 1(f)) and significantly thinned in the normal direction (ND) with an average thickness of 380 ± 90 nm.

attributes.size: 500 ± 100 nm equivalent diameter on RD-TD, 340 ± 80 nm thickness

evidence.quote: Most of the ultrafine matrix grains are also elongated along the RD, yielding an average equivalent diameter of 500 ± 100 nm. The grain thickness of the UFG matrix (340 ± 80 nm) is slightly smaller than that of the large lamellar-shaped grains.
The average diameter and the number density of the NPs obtained by TEM are 3.1 ± 1.3 nm and 2.0 × 10^23 m–3, respectively, yielding a volume fraction of 0.3 %.

By comparison, both the RD-ND and TD-ND planes reveal a near linear alignment of oxides, forming oxide bands along the extended PPBs. The spacing of oxide bands is in the range of several micrometers.
The OM image of the HPed heterostructural alloy (Fig. S3(a)) clearly shows the preliminary powder boundaries (PPBs), which are decorated by many coarse particles (~ 100 nm in diameter, Fig. S3(b)).
Sub-boundaries with a misorientation angle between 2° and 15° are marked with white dashed lines.
A further examination reveals a well-developed dimpled microstructure within the delamination bands (Fig. 4(b)). However, the dimples are rather shallow, and their size is similar to the grain size.
The crack with a stepped pattern penetrates into the matrix, and the step height is in the range of several micrometers, in good agreement with the spacing of the oxide bands.
